quick.intro: Enter a floor or a number range to generate -- the app will translate it into the window width and window count in the form below (window width capped at 10,000,000).
quick.hint_floor: If the floor doesn't exist yet, it will be created. Width is a multiple of 10 million (1 = 10M, max 1000 = 10B) -- the requested amount is always rounded up to whole windows, on-disk files stay the same predictable size. Empty starting point = continue from the last existing file (then type the Floor field yourself); a given starting point determines the floor for you (the field becomes read-only) and sets a LITERAL target -- the app checks whether [starting point, starting point + width) is already in storage and reports that instead of regenerating it; if only part is missing, it generates just that part.
quick.hint_range: Both fields are required, From cannot be greater than or equal to To, minimum value for From is 0. Python-style formats allowed, e.g. 10**5. The range is rounded out to whole windows: From rounded down, To rounded up to the nearest multiple of 10,000,000 (e.g. 12M..309M -> 10M..310M). Must fit within a single floor -- the engine generates one floor at a time. If the given range is already fully in storage, the app will say so; if only partially, it will generate the missing part (from the last existing file through the end of the requested range).
quick.explore_auto_floor_empty: Nothing has been generated yet anywhere in this database -- type a floor yourself to start exploring one.
quick.hint_explore: Leave Floor blank (or click its own "Auto (highest floor)" button, which fills it in explicitly) to continue from wherever the deepest generated data in the whole database currently sits -- re-detected fresh every time, so pressing Generate repeatedly with nothing typed keeps extending whatever is genuinely deepest right now. Type a floor yourself to explore a specific one instead; this mode only ever continues an EXISTING floor (it never creates a new one), so a completely empty database still needs one typed by hand. A low floor (0-6, 0 is a real floor here, not a stand-in for blank) is a small, fixed range shared by all of them together: if it isn't fully generated yet, one click fills it completely (Iterations/Width don't apply to it) and stops there; if it's ALREADY fully generated, this mode automatically rolls forward to floor 7 instead and continues using the Iterations/Width you asked for -- there's nothing left below floor 7 to explore, ever. Width is a multiple of 10 million PER iteration (1 = 10M, max 1000 = 10B, same meaning as Floor only's) -- size it to the available RAM (see ITS OWN Auto button, further right). Number of iterations is how many times that width gets added in a row (max 100).
quick.hint_primesieve: Floor + From + Width, not From/To -- From is a literal starting point (like Floor mode's own Starting point field), Width is a multiple of 10 million added to it (same [1, 1000] meaning as Floor/Exploration mode's Width). Floor is independent of From -- type a floor and click Auto to fill From with wherever that floor's storage currently ends, without having to work out a huge resume number by hand; leaving From blank and just entering a Floor does the same thing automatically when you click Generate. Generation runs through libprimesieve's own primesieve_generate_primes() directly, with no batching/orchestrator of ours involved -- the fastest way to fill a range, within libprimesieve's own uint64 limit (up to 18,446,744,073,709,551,615). Requesting anything past that limit truncates the result to it; use Floor, Range, or Exploration mode instead for numbers beyond it (slower, but with no such ceiling).

quick.auto_ram_result:
Available RAM in WSL: {available_gb} GB.
Recommended maximum window count for one run: {recommended} (= {numbers_total} numbers).

This is a conservative estimate based only on the shared sieve output buffer -- the per-process overhead (which grows with floor depth) isn't accounted for. Check the peak RAM column in the benchmark log after a first run and adjust if needed.

quick.attribution_primesieve: This mode calls libprimesieve, an independent open-source project by Kim Walisch (github.com/kimwalisch/primesieve, BSD license) -- directly, with no custom engine of ours in between. See the Generation README for details.

quick.error_primesieve_from_required: Enter a starting point (From), or enter a Floor -- with From left blank, Generate continues automatically from wherever that floor's storage currently ends (its own start if nothing is there yet).
